content.text:
## Findings

**Drop 1 (bars 33–48) and Drop 2 (bars 57–72) run almost the full track list at once.** Everything that was already in the build stays in, and the drop layers more on top.

### What’s stacked in the drop
| Layer | Tracks on | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Low end | Kick, Sub, Mid Bass | Kick −12.6 LUFS / sub band −10; Sub −14.2 / sub −8.5 — healthy |
| Drums | Clap, Hats, Ride | Hats + Ride both fill the top continuously |
| Hook | Lead + Lead 2 | Same rhythm, octave apart, both 7-voice supersaws |
| Mid fill | Arp, Pad, Vox Chops | All sitting in the same mid band as the leads |

### Midrange pile-up (the actual crowding)
Spectral **mid 400–2 kHz** in the drop:
- **Lead** −12 dB (E4–B4 hook) — loudest mid source, −14 LUFS
- **Pad** −13 dB (E3–E4 wholes, width 0.85) — −15 LUFS, never leaves after bar 17
- **Lead 2** −14 dB (E5–B5, same hook shape)
- **Vox Chops** −14 dB
- **Arp** −15.5 dB (E4–D5 16ths — same register as Lead)
- **Mid Bass** −17 dB (distorted, saturator drive 8 dB)

Lead, Arp, and Pad occupy the same pitch/register zone. Lead and Lead 2 are the same melodic contour an octave apart, both dense supersaws. EQ on those tracks is only a highpass (Lead 180 Hz, Lead 2 250 Hz, Pad 150 Hz, Vox 220 Hz) — no mid scooping between them.

### Arrangement issues (not just mix)
- **Pad** clip is bars 17–48, then 49–72 — full level through build, drop 1, break, and drop 2. No drop contrast.
- **Arp** clip is bars 17–48 and 57–72 — build material that never steps out for the hook.
- **Hats** (offbeat 8ths, high band −16.5) + **Ride** (quarters, high −18) double the high-end pulse the whole drop.
- Master limiter is already averaging **4.5 dB GR**, so the stacked mid energy is getting squashed together rather than separating.

Low end (kick/sub/mid bass) is not the problem. The crowd is melodic/mid + two metallic tops that never take turns.

---

## Proposal

Concrete edits, ordered by impact. Do 1–3 first; 4–5 if it still feels thick.

1. **Pad › arrangement** — Shorten/split so pad is **out of both drops**: keep pad in build (17–32) and break (49–56); remove (or mute) pad clips covering bars 33–48 and 57–72. Biggest single unmask of the hook.

2. **Arp › arrangement** — Remove arp from the drops: end the first arp clip at bar 33 (build only), and delete/mute the arp clip at bars 57–72. Stops 16th-note E4–D5 fighting Lead’s E4–B4.

3. **Lead 2 › arrangement (call/response, don’t delete the part)** — In drop 1, keep Lead 2 only on bars 41–48 (second half). In drop 2, keep Lead 2 only on bars 65–72. First 8 bars of each drop = Lead alone; second 8 = both. Cuts continuous double-supersaw density without losing the octave hook.

4. **Ride › mixer** — Mute Ride in drop 1 (bars 33–48), leave Hats. In drop 2, either mute Hats and keep Ride, or set Ride volume to **−18 dB** (from −12) so one metal top leads each drop.

5. **Vox Chops › mixer + EQ** — Drop volume from **−6 dB → −10 dB**. On Vox › EQ Eight, add a cut: **peak −4 dB at 1.2 kHz, Q ≈ 1.2** so chops sit under the lead mid peak instead of matching it (−14 dB mid band).

6. **Optional glue if you keep Pad in the break only** — Already covered by (1). If you insist on a touch of pad in the drop, use volume **−14 dB** (from −6.5) and EQ Eight low-mid cut **−5 dB at 400 Hz, Q ≈ 0.8** — but full remove in the drop is cleaner.

No changes proposed to Kick, Sub, Mid Bass, Clap, or Lead 1 levels/MIDI — those are the drop’s spine and measure fine. After 1–3 the limiter should also work less hard because less constant mid energy is hitting it.
